_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Belrise Industries (consolidated; Rs crore). Revenue has two lines with very different margins: manufacturing (sheet-metal, chassis, exhaust, polymer, suspension and other parts; 81% of FY26 revenue, 13.7% EBITDA margin) and trading of goods (steel and other goods sold mainly outside India; 19%, ~5% margin). The engine takes one growth rate and one margin, so the two-line build is kept in lineBuild and checked against model revenue and EBITDA in BELRISE.ctx.js. Share count and Mar-26 balance sheet are pro forma for the Jul-2026 QIP (BELRISE.patch.js). The pending merger of the two promoter companies (BAPL, EITSPL) is NOT in the base: it still needed NCLT approval on 30-Sep-2026 (shown as a sensitivity). Valued on P/E, as the street does.
_revenueWhy: Sum of the two lines in lineBuild. Manufacturing +18% / +16% / +15%: Q1FY27 +20% (Q4FY26 +21%); orders won in FY26-27 start in Q2-Q4FY27 (exhaust and fuel tank for a fast-growing 2W/3W OEM ~Rs90 cr a year, chassis Rs65 cr and Rs50 cr, solar-tracker assemblies up to Rs150 cr at peak, a 4W EV localisation programme, brakes and suspensions); the Hyva tipper business (bought for Rs54 cr, closing Q3FY27) adds from H2; 4W/CV doubling target. Trading -3% / +5% / +5%: Q1FY27 -19% (Middle East disruption), management expects recovery but slower than manufacturing. Management guidance: mid-teens revenue growth (May and Aug-2026 calls).

lineBuild._why: FY26 from the Q4FY26 presentation (p7-8, 16): manufacturing revenue Rs7,734.6 cr (EBITDA Rs1,057.7 cr, 13.7%), trading Rs1,774.5 cr (EBITDA Rs96.1 cr = total Rs1,153.8 cr less manufacturing), total Rs9,509.1 cr. Q1FY27: manufacturing Rs2,197.9 cr at 12.7%, trading Rs348.6 cr at 4.0%.

_marginWhy: Blended from lineBuild. Manufacturing 13.2% in FY27 (Q1 12.7%: steel and polymer cost lag, the April wage increments and minimum-wage hike, staff hired ahead of four new plants; management says the cost pain is behind it and margins rise in the coming quarters), 13.5% / 13.6% in FY28-29 as new plants fill and SDM (France) turns EBITDA positive, still below FY25's 13.9%. Trading 4.5% (FY25 6.1%, FY26 5.4%, Q1FY27 4.0%). Group margin 11.8% in FY27 vs 12.1% in FY26: in line with JM Financial (11.8%) and with management's 'broadly stable' guidance only if trading stays small.
_capexWhy: Guidance: capex 6-6.5% of manufacturing revenue (Q4FY26 call, incl. R&D). 6.25% of our manufacturing revenue plus Rs54 cr for the Hyva tipper business in FY27. FY26 capex Rs486 cr (company), Rs618 cr of fixed assets purchased in the cash-flow statement. Further acquisitions from the QIP money (management intends to deploy most of it in FY27) are not modelled: targets and prices are unknown.
_depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs361 cr = 6.9% of average gross block (Rs5,210 cr); Q1FY27 Rs99 cr (~Rs395 cr annualised).
_treasuryWhy: Applied by the engine to net cash (cash + investments - borrowings incl. leases). Pro forma Mar-26 net cash ~Rs1,090 cr after the Rs1,657 cr net QIP proceeds (net debt Rs598 cr before it). Bank deposits / liquid funds ~6.5%. Includes Rs113 cr of unlisted equity investments (Rs99 cr in BAPL) that earn nothing: overstates other income by ~Rs7 cr a year.
_otherIncomeWhy: Non-treasury other income: FY26 Rs110 cr = interest Rs45 cr (IPO cash parked before the Jun-2025 debt repayment), miscellaneous Rs53 cr (incl. scrap and incentives), FX gain Rs11 cr, rent Rs1 cr (AR FY26 note 28). Q1FY27 Rs18 cr; the four quarters to Jun-2026 Rs99 cr. Rs55 cr in FY27 (Q1 plus ~Rs12 cr a quarter), Rs50 cr after; FX gains not repeated.
_interestWhy: FY26 Rs232 cr (IPO repaid Rs1,596 cr of debt in Jun-2025); Q1FY27 Rs46 cr on ~Rs1,500 cr of gross debt incl. leases and bill discounting. Part of the QIP repays debt (Rs532 cr deployed by 30-Sep-2026, mainly debt repayment and vendor payments, per CRISIL): ~Rs43 cr a quarter from Q2.
_taxWhy: FY26 effective 25.4% (Rs169 cr on Rs666 cr), Q1FY27 26.9%; new regime 25.17% plus some non-deductible items.
_payoutWhy: FY26 final dividend Rs0.55 a share (~Rs49 cr on 89 cr shares, ~10% of profit; Screener payout 10%). First dividend as a listed company; no stated policy.

dcf._betaWhy: Two-wheeler-heavy auto supplier (82% of manufacturing revenue), cyclical, with net cash after the QIP: beta 1.0, cost of equity 12.5%, used as the discount rate.
dcf._tgWhy: Indian vehicle production ~5-6% plus content gains; house range 5-6%: 6%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~13.5% in FY29E to 8%.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: Group EBITDA margin drifts to 12.5% as trading shrinks in the mix.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex ~5% of total revenue (6-6.5% of manufacturing revenue) in the long run; depreciation ~3.8% of revenue (FY26 3.8%).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: The new 2W/3W customers and the 4W/CV programmes ramp as guided, the solar and aerospace lines scale, trading recovers, and manufacturing margins return to ~14%; the QIP money buys earnings-accretive businesses.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Two-wheeler demand fades after the GST-cut boost, the largest customer keeps losing share, steel and wage costs are recovered late, trading stays weak and the acquired aerospace units keep losing money.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Belrise: P/E on FY28E EPS (Jefferies and JM Financial 26x FY28E, May-2026). Multiple derived in BELRISE.ctx.js (own forward P/E median over the 12 months to 30-Sep-2026 x the same-window auto-component sector move) and written by BELRISE.val.js.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Own trailing EV/EBITDA median over the same 12 months with the same sector move, restated to Sep-28E EBITDA.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, cost of equity 12.5%, terminal growth 6%.
